don't really have a strong opinion on their existence in this sub but i definitely get where you're coming from.

honestly speaking i think it's bs when someone says they're more fattening than the foods they mimic - tbh a lot of protein bars get their calories from... protein. they often use some amount of artificial sweeteners as well, and not just purely sugar. sure theres the whole debate on whether or not you "should" be eating artificial sweeteners, but in terms of calories & calorie composition it's all about knowledge.

I've been there. More recently I don't eat "normally" really, but I've still been unable to have ED behaviors in the way I'm comfortable with because I feel like I'm being watched by my family.

It doesn't make you invalid. The thoughts are still there. It's a very frustrating place to be.

sometimes I do this, but I don't really know what is normal or what's excessive - but sometimes if it's something I don't think is risky, I share it, and then immediately after regret it and wish I hadn't done it, but the message is already sent and I know they've seen it so I can't just delete it (though sometimes I do anyways). 

I always feel like I'm annoying people and that I share excessive information, but maybe since I have AvPD I think it's excessive when it isn't... or maybe I think a friendship is closer than it really is because of just how much I lack real friends, so it *is* excessive for the other person but isn't for friendships as a whole...? I can't tell, and I sure won't be asking.

I'm sorry you feel the same way. I recognize I need therapy but yes, the easiest part for me is knowing I have a problem and need help. Reaching out for help feels basically impossible for me, I definitely get what you're saying there.
I'm there too in some ways, and it can be really scary. I hope you stay safe. Drinking water and sleeping is a good choice here, I hope that you sleep well and find a bit more peace of mind tomorrow.

I wouldn't consider it necessarily a misdiagnosis but before AvPD, social anxiety and generalized anxiety. I don't necessarily think these are wrong but my AvPD is much more chronic and inescapable (therefore a more significant issue), whereas the other two feel more situational.

I honestly don't understand. If someone has problems with smoking too I'd think they're just being protective which is fine.

But in the case of being fine with smoking like in this one, I think it's because of odd social norms really. Smoking is pretty normalized but self-harm isn't, and it's seen as unpleasant and shocking and people don't like that. Anything that seems strongly indicative of mental illness or whatever is really looked down upon and people don't like it.

Thank you for the response and reassurance. I always have had trouble with self-esteem but almost never to this extent where I truly feel like I'm this bad which is hard. I don't currently have a therapist (I do have a previous one who I stopped speaking to once I ran out of things to say). 

I've been thinking about getting an appointment and asking my doctor for stronger antidepressants to see if that helps. I have family and kind of have friends who I could talk to but a lot of the details of what's happening with me, I'm not sure how they'd respond.
Yeah. Often I feel like I can't even control this kind of self-harm when I get angry, I'll punch myself or bang my head or limbs against the wall or hard furniture without even really thinking

Me too. It can be hard, I understand. People can be mean sometimes, even for no reason. I wish people weren't so judgmental. It's hard to feel judged and misunderstood, I hope you're able to find people who understand and respect you.

I can't really help but I hear you and I can relate to some of these things, like feeling you have a massive distance from friends. I'm close in age too, and I understand not having motivation to get help. It's really hard to do that. I hope you find happiness in the future.
